subject: math
title: Increasing and Decreasing Patterns
seo_title: Grade 4 Increasing and Decreasing Patterns Worksheets: Pattern Rules, Tables and Input/Output (BC Math)
standard_text: Increasing and decreasing patterns, using tables and charts
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on increasing and decreasing patterns: find pattern rules for numbers to 10 000, extend shape patterns with tables, solve input/output tables and rule boxes, and predict later terms in real-life patterns. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the BC curriculum and good FSA practice.
key_big: A pattern rule tells where to start and what to do each time.
key_sub: Find the jump and check it works every time: 1015, 1040, 1065 is “start at 1015 and add 25 each time.” In an input/output table, use the rule on the In number in the same column. For the 10th term, there are 9 jumps from the 1st.
body_html:
Increasing and decreasing patterns

In an increasing pattern, the numbers get bigger. In a decreasing pattern, they get smaller. Find the jump between two numbers next to each other. Then check that the same jump works every time.

A pattern rule tells where to start and what to do each time.

Shape patterns and tables

Count each figure. Put the figure number in the top row and the count in the bottom row.

Figure number1234
Number of sticks471013

The rule is start at 4 and add 3 each time.

Input/output tables and rule boxes

A rule box changes each In number into an Out number. Use the rule on the In number in the same column.

To find a missing In number, work backward. Undo × with ÷, and undo + with −.

Find the rule

In: 2, 3, 5, 6. Out: 4, 6, 10, 12.

“Add 2” works for 2 → 4 only. Check every column: 2 × 2 = 4, 3 × 2 = 6, 5 × 2 = 10, 6 × 2 = 12.

Answer: Multiply by 2

Predict the 10th number

Start at 15 and add 4 each time. What is the 10th number?

From the 1st number to the 10th there are 9 jumps. 9 × 4 = 36. 15 + 36 = 51.

Answer: 51

A candle gets shorter

A candle is 24 cm tall. It burns 3 cm each hour. How tall is it after 5 hours?

Subtract 3 each hour: 24, 21, 18, 15, 12, 9.

Answer: 9 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using only the first step: 3, 4, 6, 9 is “add 1”Check every jump: +1, +2, +3, so the next jump is +4
Mixing up the figure number and the countThe figure number is on top. The count is below it
Extending the wrong way: 50, 45, 40, then 45A decreasing pattern keeps getting smaller
Using the start as the jump: 8, 14, 20 is “add 8”Start at 8 and add 6 each time
10 jumps for the 10th numberFrom the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps
Reading along the Out row in an In/Out tableUse the rule on the In number in the same column

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about patterns in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum, Grade 4 students work with increasing and decreasing patterns, show them in tables and charts, and describe the pattern rule. They also explore algebraic relationships, such as input/output tables and one-step equations.

faq.q: What is the difference between an increasing and a decreasing pattern?
faq.a: In an increasing pattern the numbers get bigger each time, like 15, 19, 23. In a decreasing pattern they get smaller, like 200, 185, 170.

faq.q: How do you find the rule in an input/output table?
faq.a: Compare each In number with the Out number below it and test the rule on every column, not just the first. For In 2, 3, 5 and Out 4, 6, 10, the rule is multiply by 2.

faq.q: Are patterns on the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: The Grade 4 FSA numeracy component is based on the BC curriculum, and patterning is part of Grade 4 math. Practice with pattern rules, tables and input/output problems is good preparation.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before. 24 + 4 = 28. 25 only adds 1.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before. 50 + 5 = 55.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before. 150 + 10 = 160. Only the tens digit changes.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 7 more than the one before. 27 + 7 = 34. Check the jump: 13 − 6 = 7, not 6.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 250 more than the one before. 750 + 250 = 1000. Four 250s make 1000.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 more than the one before. 550 + 25 = 575. Counting by 25s, the numbers end in 00, 25, 50 or 75.

c: Start at 8 and add 6 each time
Start at 14 and add 6 each time
Start at 8 and add 8 each time
Start at 6 and add 6 each time
items.e: 8 + 6 = 14, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 8 and add 6 each time. 8 is where the pattern starts. It is not the jump.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 1400 + 100 = 1500. Only the hundreds digit changes. 2400 changes the thousands digit.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1000 more than the one before. 4025 + 1000 = 5025. Only the thousands digit changes.

c: Start at 300 and add 100 each time
Start at 300 and add 300 each time
Start at 150 and add 150 each time
Start at 300 and add 150 each time
items.e: 300 + 150 = 450, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 300 and add 150 each time.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is +40. Go back one step from 540: 540 − 40 = 500. Going back means subtract, not add.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 more than the one before. 2000 + 25 = 2025. 2050 adds 50, not 25.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 1015 and add 25 each time
Start at 1015 and add 15 each time
Start at 1040 and add 25 each time
Start at 1015 and add 20 each time
items.e: 1015 + 25 = 1040, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 1015 and add 25 each time. 1040 − 1015 = 25.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 9900 + 100 = 10 000. 99 hundreds + 1 hundred = 100 hundreds. Write it with a space: 10 000. 1000 is missing a zero.

items.q: Which pattern follows the rule “Start at 150 and add 75 each time”?
What number comes next?
items.e: The jumps are +1, +2, +3, +4. Each jump is 1 more than the last, so the next jump is +5. 13 + 5 = 18. 14 uses only the first step (+1). 17 adds +4 again.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: The jumps are +5, +10, +20. Each number is double the one before: 40 × 2 = 80. 45 uses only the first step (+5).

items.q: Olivia counts by 250s from 0: 0, 250, 500, 750, 1000 … Which number will she say?
items.e: Counting by 250s from 0, every number ends in 000, 250, 500 or 750. Only 2250 ends that way. 2025 ends in 25, not 250.

items.q: One number in this pattern is wrong. Which one?
What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 less than the one before. 35 − 5 = 30. The numbers get smaller, so do not go back up to 40.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 8 less than the one before. 72 − 8 = 64.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 less than the one before. 700 − 100 = 600. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 less than the one before. 925 − 25 = 900. 875 subtracts 50, not 25.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 84 and add 7 each time
Start at 84 and subtract 6 each time
Start at 84 and subtract 7 each time
Start at 77 and subtract 7 each time
items.e: 84 − 7 = 77, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 84 and subtract 7 each time. The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 500 less than the one before. 3500 − 500 = 3000. 4000 goes the wrong way.

items.q: What number is missing?
What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1000 less than the one before. 6250 − 1000 = 5250. Only the thousands digit changes.

items.q: Start at 1200. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Count back by 150s 3 times: 1050, 900, 750. 1650 goes the wrong way.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 2400 and subtract 100 each time
Start at 2200 and subtract 200 each time
Start at 2400 and add 200 each time
Start at 2400 and subtract 200 each time
items.e: 2400 − 200 = 2200, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 2400 and subtract 200 each time.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 less than the one before. 2805 − 100 = 2705. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is −50. Go back one step from 630: 630 + 50 = 680. The pattern goes down, so the number before 630 is bigger.

items.q: How does this pattern change?
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so the pattern is decreasing. 5000 − 250 = 4750, 4750 − 250 = 4500. It is decreasing by 250 each time.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1000 less than the one before. 8000 − 1000 = 7000. 9000 goes the wrong way. 7900 subtracts only 100.

items.q: Start at 3000. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Count back by 500s 4 times: 2500, 2000, 1500, 1000. 1500 is only 3 jumps.

items.q: Which pattern follows the rule “Start at 2000 and subtract 250 each time”?
One number in this pattern is wrong. Which one?
Which two numbers are missing, in order?
items.e: The rule is −120. 840 − 120 = 720 and 600 − 120 = 480. The missing numbers are 720, 480. 740, 500 subtracts only 100. Write the numbers in order from left to right.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: The jumps are −10, −9, −8. Each jump is 1 less, so the next jump is −7. 73 − 7 = 66. 63 uses only the first step (−10).

items.q: Hana counts back by 25s from 1000: 1000, 975, 950 … Which number will she say?
items.e: Counting back by 25s from 1000, every number ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75: 925, 900, 875. 860, 905 and 940 do not end that way.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. Each figure has 2 more tiles. 5 + 2 = 7 tiles in Figure 4.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure has 2 more sticks. 7 + 2 = 9 sticks in Figure 4. Count the sticks, not the triangles.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. Each figure has 3 more sticks. 10 + 3 = 13 sticks in Figure 4. 16 counts 4 sticks for every square, but squares next to each other share a stick.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 12, 10, 8. Each figure has 2 fewer tiles. 8 − 2 = 6 tiles in Figure 4. This pattern is decreasing, so do not add.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure has 2 more chairs. 8 + 2 = 10 chairs in Figure 4. 16 counts 4 chairs for every table, but no chairs fit where tables touch.

items.q: In this table, 18 is under 5. What does that mean?
items.e: Read down the column. The figure number is on top and the number of cubes is below. So Figure 5 has 18 cubes.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of sticks?
c: Start at 4 and add 4 each time
Start at 3 and add 3 each time
Start at 4 and add 3 each time
Start at 1 and add 3 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 4 sticks. Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. The pattern rule is start at 4 and add 3 each time. 4 is how many sticks Figure 1 has. It is not the jump.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of chairs?
c: Start at 4 and add 6 each time
Start at 4 and add 2 each time
Start at 2 and add 2 each time
Start at 4 and add 4 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 4 chairs. Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. The pattern rule is start at 4 and add 2 each time.

items.q: This table shows a shape pattern. How many sticks are in Figure 6?
items.e: The table goes up by 3 each time. Keep going: 13, 16, 19. Figure 6 has 19 sticks. 24 is 6 × 4, but the jump is 3, not 4.

items.q: This table shows a shape pattern. How many sticks are in Figure 8?
items.e: The table goes up by 2 each time. Keep going: 9, 11, 13, 15, 17. Figure 8 has 17 sticks. 15 is Figure 7.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of tiles?
c: Start at 12 and subtract 2 each time
Start at 12 and subtract 1 each time
Start at 10 and subtract 2 each time
Start at 12 and add 2 each time
items.e: Figure 1 has 12 tiles. Count each figure: 12, 10, 8. The pattern rule is start at 12 and subtract 2 each time. The pattern gets smaller, so the rule subtracts.

items.q: This table shows a shape pattern. How many cubes are in Figure 7?
items.e: The table goes up by 3 each time. Keep going: 15, 18, 21, 24. Figure 7 has 24 cubes. 21 is Figure 6.

items.q: What number is missing from the table?
items.e: The number of dots goes up by 5 each time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. The missing number is 20. 4 is the figure number, not the number of dots.

items.q: Figure 2 is hidden. How many sticks are in Figure 2?
items.e: Figure 1 has 3 sticks and Figure 3 has 7 sticks. The pattern grows by the same amount each time: 3, 5, 7. The rule is add 2.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 22 sticks?
items.e: Keep going: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22. Figure 7 has 22 sticks. 22 is the number of sticks, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 20 chairs?
items.e: Keep going: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. Figure 9 has 20 chairs. 20 is the number of chairs, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 10?
items.e: Start at 4 and add 3 each time. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 9 × 3 = 27. 4 + 27 = 31. 34 makes 10 jumps. 40 is 10 × 4.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 10?
items.e: Start at 3 and add 2 each time. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 9 × 2 = 18. 3 + 18 = 21. 30 counts 3 sticks for every triangle, but triangles share sticks.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 6?
items.e: Start at 12 and subtract 2 each time: 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2. Figure 6 has 2 tiles. 22 goes the wrong way. 0 makes one jump too many.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 5?
items.e: Count: 1, 3, 6. The jumps are +2, +3, so the next jumps are +4 and +5: 6, 10, 15. 9 uses only the first step (+2) each time.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 7 into the rule: 7 + 5 = 12. 35 multiplies instead of adding.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 6 into the rule: 6 × 4 = 24. 10 adds 4 instead of multiplying.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 30 into the rule: 30 − 8 = 22. 38 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 45 into the rule: 45 ÷ 5 = 9. 40 subtracts 5 instead of dividing.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 250 into the rule: 250 + 100 = 350. Adding 100 changes the hundreds digit.

items.q: The rule is Multiply by 6. Which In → Out pair follows the rule?
items.e: 8 × 6 = 48, so 8 → 48 follows the rule. 8 → 14 adds 6. 8 → 56 is 8 × 7. 6 × 6 is 36, not 42.

items.q: What number went in?
items.e: Work backward. Undo + 9 with − 9: 30 − 9 = 21. Check: 21 + 9 = 30. 39 adds 9 again.

items.q: The rule is Multiply by 3. What is the missing Out number?
items.e: Use the rule on the In number above the ?: 7 × 3 = 21. 18 adds 3 to the last Out number, but the In numbers do not go up by 1.

items.q: The rule is Add 15. What is the missing Out number?
items.e: Use the rule on the In number above the ?: 40 + 15 = 55. 45 adds 5 to the last Out number. Use the rule on 40.

items.q: What number went in?
items.e: Work backward. Undo × 3 with ÷ 3: 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Check: 9 × 3 = 27. 81 multiplies again instead of undoing.

items.q: What is the rule for this table?
items.e: Look at each In number and the Out number below it: 2 × 2 = 4, 3 × 2 = 6, 5 × 2 = 10, 6 × 2 = 12. The rule is Multiply by 2. “Add 2” works for 2 → 4 only. Check every column: 3 + 2 is 5, not 6.

items.q: What is the rule for this table?
items.e: Look at each In number and the Out number below it: 3 + 7 = 10, 5 + 7 = 12, 8 + 7 = 15, 10 + 7 = 17. The rule is Add 7. “Add 2” only describes how the Out row changes from 10 to 12.

items.q: What number went in?
items.e: Work backward. Undo − 40 with + 40: 75 + 40 = 115. Check: 115 − 40 = 75. 35 subtracts again instead of undoing.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 1200 into the rule: 1200 + 350 = 1550. Add 3 hundreds and 5 tens: 1200 + 300 + 50.

items.q: What is the rule for this table?
items.e: Look at each In number and the Out number below it: 20 − 5 = 15, 30 − 5 = 25, 45 − 5 = 40, 60 − 5 = 55. The rule is Subtract 5. The Out numbers are smaller, so the rule makes numbers smaller.

items.q: What number comes out?
items.e: Put 5000 into the rule: 5000 − 1250 = 3750. 6250 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: What is the rule for this table?
items.e: Look at each In number and the Out number below it: 12 ÷ 6 = 2, 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 24 ÷ 6 = 4, 36 ÷ 6 = 6. The rule is Divide by 6. “Subtract 10” works for the first column only: 18 − 10 is 8, not 3.

items.q: The rule is Multiply by 5. What is the missing In number?
items.e: Which number times 5 is 35? Work backward: 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Check: 7 × 5 = 35. 6 only looks at the In row (2, 4, 6). 175 multiplies 35 by 5.

items.q: The rule is Multiply by 10. What is the missing Out number?
items.e: Use the rule on the In number above the ?: 25 × 10 = 250. 130 adds 10 to the last Out number. 2500 multiplies by 100.

items.q: The number goes through both rules, in order. What number comes out?
items.e: First 6 × 3 = 18. Then 18 + 4 = 22. 30 does the rules in the wrong order: (6 + 4) × 3. 18 forgets the second rule.

sets.title: Predict later terms and real-life patterns

items.q: The rule is “Start at 15 and add 4 each time.” What is the 10th number?
items.e: From the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps. 9 × 4 = 36. 15 + 36 = 51. 55 makes 10 jumps, one too many.

items.q: Liam has $12. He saves $5 each week. How much money does he have after 6 weeks?
items.e: Start at $12 and add $5 each week: $17, $22, $27, $32, $37, $42. $30 forgets the $12 he started with.

items.q: A candle gets shorter as it burns. How tall is it after 5 hours?
items.e: The candle gets 3 cm shorter each hour: 24, 21, 18, 15, 12, 9 cm. 39 cm goes the wrong way. 12 cm is after 4 hours.

items.q: The rule is “Start at 200 and subtract 15 each time.” What is the 10th number?
items.e: From the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps. 9 × 15 = 135. 200 − 135 = 65. 50 makes 10 jumps. 335 goes the wrong way.

items.q: Kai counts salmon swimming up a creek near Nanaimo. He sees 40 on Monday, 55 on Tuesday and 70 on Wednesday. The pattern continues. How many does he see on Friday?
items.e: Add 15 each day: Monday 40, Tuesday 55, Wednesday 70, Thursday 85, Friday 100. 85 is Thursday.

items.q: A Grade 4 class raises money for the Terry Fox Run. They have $60 after week 1, $95 after week 2 and $130 after week 3. The pattern continues. How much do they have after week 6?
items.e: The rule is add $35 each week: $60, $95, $130, $165, $200, $235. After week 6 they have $235. $210 is 6 × $35, but the class started at $60.

items.q: On a summer day, a BC Ferries ship leaves Horseshoe Bay at 7:20 a.m., 9:20 a.m. and 11:20 a.m. The pattern continues. When does the 5th ferry leave?
items.e: Add 2 hours each time: 7:20 a.m., 9:20 a.m., 11:20 a.m., 1:20 p.m., 3:20 p.m. After noon, the times are p.m. 1:20 p.m. is the 4th ferry.

items.q: In spring, the snow on a mountain near Whistler is 180 cm deep. It melts 15 cm each week. How deep is the snow after 6 weeks?
items.e: Subtract 15 cm each week: 180 cm, 165 cm, 150 cm, 135 cm, 120 cm, 105 cm, 90 cm. After 6 weeks it is 90 cm. 270 cm goes the wrong way. 105 cm is after 5 weeks.

items.q: It rains all day in Vancouver. The table shows the total rain. The pattern continues. How much rain is there after 8 hours?
items.e: Add 3 mm each hour. From hour 1 to hour 8 there are 7 jumps: 7 × 3 = 21. 4 + 21 = 25 mm. 24 is 8 × 3, but hour 1 already has 4 mm.

items.q: A SkyTrain comes every 6 minutes. The first three trains come at 8:04 a.m., 8:10 a.m. and 8:16 a.m. When does the 6th train come?
items.e: From the 1st to the 6th train there are 5 jumps of 6 minutes. 5 × 6 = 30. 8:04 + 30 minutes = 8:34 a.m. 8:40 a.m. makes 6 jumps.

items.q: A rain barrel holds 180 L of water. Emma uses 12 L each day to water her garden. How much water is left after 7 days?
items.e: She uses 7 × 12 = 84 L. 180 − 84 = 96 L. 84 L is the water she used, not what is left. 264 L goes the wrong way.

items.q: Ava makes a bead pattern. Figure 1 has 7 beads. Each figure has 7 more beads than the one before. Which figure has 63 beads?
items.e: Count by 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63. That is Figure 9. 63 is the number of beads, not the figure number.

items.q: Simran has $20. She saves $16 each week. After how many weeks will she have $100?
items.e: Count on by $16: $36, $52, $68, $84, $100. That is 5 weeks. 6 weeks counts one week too many.

items.q: Picnic tables at Stanley Park are pushed together in a row. How many people can sit at 8 tables?
items.e: Start at 4 and add 2 for each table: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. 8 tables seat 18 people. 32 counts 4 seats for every table, but no one sits where tables touch.

items.q: A cedar seedling is 30 cm tall. It grows 15 cm each year. How tall is it after 8 years?
items.e: 8 years means 8 jumps of 15 cm: 8 × 15 = 120. 30 + 120 = 150 cm. 120 cm forgets the 30 cm it started with. 165 cm is after 9 years.

items.q: Mei bikes on the Stanley Park Seawall. She bikes 3 km in week 1, 5 km in week 2 and 7 km in week 3. The pattern continues. How far does she bike in week 10?
items.e: Add 2 km each week. From week 1 to week 10 there are 9 jumps: 9 × 2 = 18. 3 + 18 = 21 km. 23 km makes 10 jumps. 30 km is 10 × 3.

items.q: Each canoe holds 3 people. In is the number of canoes and Out is the number of people. How many people can 15 canoes hold?
items.e: The rule is Multiply by 3. 15 × 3 = 45. 18 adds 3 to 15 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Owen counts by 25s from 0. He says, “I will say 1630.” Is he right?
c: No, counting by 25s gives numbers ending in 00, 25, 50 or 75
No, he can only count to 1000
items.e: Counting by 25s from 0 gives 25, 50, 75, 100 … Every number ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75. 1630 ends in 30, so he is not right.

items.q: A bag of birdseed has 5000 g. Harjot puts 250 g in the bird feeder each day. How much birdseed is left after 12 days?
items.e: He uses 12 × 250 = 3000 g. 5000 − 3000 = 2000 g. 3000 g is how much he used. 2250 g is after 11 days.

items.q: Nadia has $0 and saves $8 each week. Ryan has $24 and saves $5 each week. After how many weeks will they have the same amount?
items.e: Make a table. Nadia: $0, $8, $16, $24, $32, $40, $48, $56, $64. Ryan: $24, $29, $34, $39, $44, $49, $54, $59, $64. After 8 weeks they both have $64. 3 weeks is when Nadia has $24, but Ryan has more by then.
